 “The guy in the leather jacket”: Host welcomes Jensen Huang's departure
News
Nov 17, 2026 01:56 PM
 Oliver Jäger 
Add as a preferred source on Google
Image Source: Nvidia, Tulane Public Relations CC BY 2.0 , mit KI überarbeitet 
 CNBC host Jim Cramer took a swipe at Jensen Huang on American television following his departure. He considers Colette Kress more capable and referred to Huang as “the guy in the leather jacket.”
 Jensen Huang is no longer Nvidia's CEO. The news shook the tech industry and Nvidia's share price a few days ago. But alongside his many supporters among employees and across the industry, the man in the leather jacket also has critics, including CNBC host and journalist Jim Cramer. On the hour-long CNN show “OutFront” with Erin Burnett, he voiced some scathing criticism of Jensen Huang and his admiration for successor Colette Kress - and drew criticism from viewers in the process.
 Jim Cramer is on Team Kress and takes aim at Jensen Huang 
 Speaking with Erin Burnett, Jim Cramer discusses his personal experiences with Colette Kress, which he says showed him that Nvidia's EVP and CFO, now interim CEO, is a formidable, tough woman. Cramer considers her more capable than Jensen Huang of running the company properly. He says she has a deeper understanding of the business and knows the company and its day-to-day operations better than Jensen Huang himself. Jim Cramer also says he has more confidence in Colette Kress than he ever had in Nvidia's longtime CEO.

 He also lashes out at Jensen Huang while speaking to Erin Burnett: “There are 49,000 people working at this company. And there's one guy in a leather jacket. That's an insult to the other 49,000, because the guy in the leather jacket is gone, and that means they're not worth anything anymore.” The CNBC host grew somewhat heated as he spoke, apparently criticizing the notion that the company's value depends largely on Jensen Huang.

 The clip was shared by the Outfront show's account on X, where it has already been viewed more than 220,000 times. Many of the more than 150 comments under the post, however, are unkind to Jim Cramer, who many feel is going too far. A large proportion question the journalist and CNBC host's expertise on the subject or simply call him a “clown.” The reactions in the comments are hardly surprising given the growing media coverage of support for Jensen Huang.
 Key takeaways 
 Following Jensen Huang's resignation, Nvidia shareholders and hardware buyers face the question of how stable the company is under interim CEO Colette Kress.
 Jim Cramer's remarks highlight the debate over how much Nvidia's success depends on Jensen Huang, and their controversial nature has sparked a strong backlash.
 For now, sympathies seem to lie more with Jensen Huang, particularly among employees , with strong calls for his reinstatement as CEO—although the extent of that support ultimately remains unverified. Out of “solidarity” with Jensen Huang and bewilderment over the circumstances surrounding his resignation, one robotics engineer even decided to leave Nvidia.
